parts.text: Some students are determining the resistance per unit length of wire X . They are using the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1. The crocodile clip is connected to a length of the resistance wire. The current in the circuit and potential difference (p.d.) across wire X are measured.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 2.1, draw the symbol for a voltmeter correctly connected to measure the p.d. across wire X . [1]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text: correct voltmeter symbol in parallel with wire X

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) A student adjusts the position of the crocodile clip until the current in the circuit is 0.80 A. In Table 2.1, record the value of the p.d. V across wire X, as shown in Fig. 2.2. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student records the p.d. V for different currents, as shown in Table 2.1. Table 2.1 I / A V / V 0.80 0.70 1.58 0.60 1.34 0.50 1.03 0.40 0.81

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Plot a graph of V / V ( y -axis) against I / A ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 2(c)(i)
ms.text:
graph:
axes labelled correct orientation, with quantity and unit
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots
well-judged line and thin line

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(c)(ii)
ms.text: G present and triangle method seen on graph

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Fig. 2.3 shows wire X . • On Fig. 2.3, measure the length l . l = ........................................................ cm • The wire in Fig. 2.3 is shown to 1/3 rd scale. Calculate the actual length L of wire X . L = ........................................................ cm [1]

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the resistance R of each centimetre of wire X , using the equation R = G × k L , where k = 1.0 Ω cm. Give the value for R , to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. R = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 2(c)(iv)
ms.text:
R in range 0.17 to 0.23
2 / 3 sig figs and unit = Ω or Ω / cm
